mainTopic: Whether the air above the מזבח counts as the מזבח, and the משנה on when כלי שרת sanctify their contents, with related rules about damaged vessels and בגדי כהונה.
overview: The amud opens by trying to prove that the air above the מזבח counts as the מזבח, since otherwise a כהן could never sprinkle blood from disqualified offerings without it 'coming down.' The idea that he presses the blood onto the wall is rejected, because that would be squeezing or pouring, not proper sprinkling. רב אשי limits the question to items hung over the מזבח on a pole, and that case ends in תיקו. A new משנה then teaches that liquid vessels sanctify only liquids, dry measures sanctify only dry items, vessels with a hole still work if they can do their usual job, and all vessels sanctify only in the עזרה. שמואל says מזרקות sanctify dry items too, and he lists conditions: vessels sanctify only when whole, full, and from inside. רבי יוחנן adds that if the כהן plans to add more, each amount becomes holy right away. רב explains that a liquid vessel makes dry items holy enough to become פסול, though not fit to offer. The amud ends with ברייתות about not repairing damaged vessels and knives and about making and washing בגדי כהונה, and אביי's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from sprinkling the blood of disqualified offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the air above the מזבח must count as the מזבח. Otherwise there would be no way to sprinkle the blood of a disqualified חטאת העוף or of other disqualified offerings that went up on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take a disqualified bird sin offering that is on the מזבח. How can the כהן sprinkle its blood? As soon as he lifts it, it should count as having come down off the מזבח! The same goes for other disqualified offerings: how can he throw their blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a proof that the airspace above the מזבח is treated like the מזבח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that disqualified items which went up on the מזבח stay there, but once they come down they don't go back up. If the air above the מזבח did not count as the מזבח, then lifting the bird or the blood to sprinkle would make it 'come down,' and sprinkling would be impossible. Since we do sprinkle, the air must count as the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling / he sprinkles (the blood action of a חטאת העוף)
Something that has gone down (off the מזבח)
Throwing the blood (the blood action of most animal offerings)

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of the argument. The hidden opening is: 'If you say the air above the מזבח is NOT like the מזבח, then...'

phrases.english: A disqualified bird sin offering
phrases.notes: He means one that already went up on the מזבח, so it stays there even though it is disqualified.

phrases.english: how does he sprinkle from its blood?
It has become something that went down!
phrases.notes: Lifting it up to sprinkle counts as taking it off the מזבח, and disqualified things that come down don't go back up.

phrases.english: Other disqualified offerings,
how does he throw from their blood?

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף פְּסוּלָה הֵיכִי מַזֶּה מִדָּמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of whether the air above the מזבח counts as the מזבח, by offering a proof.
steps.raayaObject: The airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted practice of sprinkling or throwing blood from disqualified offerings that went up on the מזבח.

steps.title: Maybe he presses the blood right against the wall
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Perhaps the כהן presses the blood directly onto the מזבח, so it never passes through the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: He presses them right against the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the blood never goes through the air at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if sprinkling requires passing through the air. If the כהן touches the blood straight to the wall, the item never leaves the מזבח area. Then the proof says nothing about the air.

keyTerms.meaning: That he makes it touch / presses it against

phrases.english: That he presses them against [the מזבח].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by suggesting a different way of applying the blood.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Undercuts the proof without deciding the main question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the blood must pass through the air, which may not be true.

steps.title: Pressing is not sprinkling or throwing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pushback. Pressing a bird's blood onto the wall is מיצוי (squeezing), not הזאה. Pressing an animal's blood is שפיכה (pouring), not זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that sprinkling? That's squeezing! Is that throwing? That's pouring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 2, saying pressing does not count as the required blood service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offering has a specific blood action. Pressing the blood against the wall turns the act into a different action, מיצוי or שפיכה. So it cannot fulfill the requirement of הזאה or זריקה, and the proof from step 1 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing out the blood against the wall

phrases.english: Is this sprinkling?! It is squeezing!
Is this throwing?! It is pouring!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback of step 2, restoring the proof of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the כהן presses the blood onto the wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pressing changes the act into a different blood action, so the required הזאה or זריקה is not done.

steps.title: And besides, that is not how it is done
steps.stepSummary: A second argument against step 2: the normal way of doing הזאה and זריקה is simply not like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, is that the way sprinkling is done? Is that the way throwing is done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another reason to reject the pressing idea: it is not the normal way the service is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even apart from what the act is called, the service must be done in its usual way. Pressing the blood is not the normal way of sprinkling or throwing. So the blood must really go through the air, and the proof that the air counts as the מזבח seems to stand.

phrases.english: And furthermore, is this the way of sprinkling?!
Is this the way of throwing?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the pushback of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The service must be done in its normal manner, and pressing is not the normal manner.

steps.title: רב אשי: the question is only about hanging on a pole
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains why the proof does not settle the question. When the כהן stands on top of the מזבח holding the items, they surely count as on the מזבח. The real question is when he hangs them over the מזבח on a pole while standing below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If he holds them while standing on top of the מזבח, then yes, they count as on the מזבח. When the question was asked, it was about a case where he hung them on a pole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows the question, so the proof from sprinkling no longer answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinkling proof only covers a כהן standing on the מזבח, where his holding the items keeps them 'on the מזבח.' That says nothing about air the כהן isn't standing over, as when he hangs items from a pole while standing on the courtyard floor. So the proof is true, but it answers a different question.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not reject the proof's logic. He agrees with it, but limits the original question to a different case.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If he holds them on top of the altar —
phrases.notes: He means the כהן himself is standing up on the מזבח while holding them.

phrases.english: indeed so [they count as on the altar];
when it was asked — it was where he hung them on a pole.
phrases.notes: Here the כהן stands on the courtyard floor and holds the items over the מזבח on a pole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אִי דְּנָקֵט לְהוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the sprinkling proof but shows it does not address the real question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the original question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof from sprinkling shows that all airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proof only covers a כהן standing on the מזבח. The open question is about items hung on a pole by someone standing below.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about items hung over the מזבח on a pole is left unanswered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? It stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the law is in the pole case and ends with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the proof is limited to a כהן standing on the מזבח, nothing else settles the pole case. So it is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן holding items while standing on the מזבח makes them count as on the מזבח. Whether the air above the מזבח counts as the מזבח when items hang there on a pole is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: What [is the law]? Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question as narrowed by רב אשי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The pole case (אויר מזבח without the כהן standing on top) remains unresolved: תיקו.

steps.title: Liquid vessels sanctify liquids, dry measures sanctify dry items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that each type of כלי שרת sanctifies only the kind of item it was made for: liquid vessels for liquids, dry measures for dry items.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Vessels made for liquids make liquids holy, and measures made for dry items make dry items holy. A liquid vessel does not make a dry item holy, and a dry vessel does not make a liquid holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches that a כלי שרת only makes holy the type of item it was designed to hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting something into a כלי שרת can give it holiness. This משנה limits that power: the item must match the vessel's purpose. A wine or oil vessel does not sanctify flour, and a flour measure does not sanctify oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels used for liquids, such as wine or oil
Measuring vessels for dry items, such as flour
They make holy, giving the item the status of קדשים

phrases.english: MISHNAH
Vessels for liquids sanctify liquids,
and dry measures sanctify dry items.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כְּלִי הַלַּח מְקַדֶּשֶׁת אֶת הַיָּבֵשׁ,
phrases.english: A liquid vessel does not sanctify dry items,
and a dry vessel does not sanctify liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the earlier question ended in תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי שרת sanctifies only the type of item (liquid or dry) it was made for.

steps.title: Vessels with holes, and sanctifying only in the holy area
steps.stepSummary: A holy vessel that got a hole still sanctifies if it can still do the same kind of job it did when whole. All vessels sanctify only inside the holy area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy vessels that got holes: if they can still be used for the kind of work they did when they were whole, they sanctify. If not, they do not. And all of them sanctify only in the holy place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more rules: what happens when a holy vessel gets a hole, and where vessels have the power to sanctify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole does not automatically cancel a vessel's power. The test is whether it can still do its usual job. The power to sanctify also works only inside the קודש area, the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy vessels used in the עבודה
Work similar to their usual job
In the holy area, the עזרה

phrases.english: Holy vessels that got a hole,
if one can do with them work like their work
that they did when they were whole –
they sanctify; and if not, they do not sanctify.
And all of them sanctify only in the holy area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more rules about when vessels sanctify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel with a hole sanctifies if it can still do its usual job. All vessels sanctify only within the קודש.

steps.title: שמואל: the rule is only about measuring vessels, since cups sanctify dry flour
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה's rule to measuring vessels. מזרקות do sanctify dry items, as the פסוק describes them full of סלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: They only taught this about measures. But cups do sanctify dry items, as it says: 'Both of them full of fine flour.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל, who says the משנה's rule (liquid vessels do not sanctify dry items) applies only to measuring vessels, not to מזרקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מזרקות are mainly used for blood, a liquid. Even so, the פסוק describes a מזרק full of flour, a dry item. So the מזרק also counts as a vessel for dry items and sanctifies them.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
They only taught this about, a phrase that limits a rule
Cups or basins, mainly used to collect blood of קרבנות
Fine flour, used for a מנחה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
They taught this only about measures,
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a liquid vessel does not sanctify dry items.

phrases.english: but cups do sanctify,
as it says: 'Both of them full of fine flour.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:13. 'Both' means the silver bowl and the silver מזרק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the first rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only liquid measures fail to sanctify dry items. מזרקות sanctify dry items too.

steps.title: But a מנחה is a liquid
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges שמואל's proof: the flour in the פסוק is a מנחה mixed with oil, so it counts as liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: A מנחה is liquid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי attacks שמואל's proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of flour mixed with oil. If that counts as liquid, the פסוק only shows that a מזרק holds liquid, so we cannot learn that it sanctifies dry items.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering, usually mixed with oil

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
A meal offering is a liquid!
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says the flour was 'mixed with oil,' so it is wet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's proof from 'both of them full of fine flour.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flour mixed with oil is wet, so the פסוק shows nothing about dry items.

steps.title: The פסוק is for the dry part of the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the פסוק teaches about the flour in the מנחה that stayed dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was needed only for the dry part in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends שמואל's proof with a first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of the flour in a מנחה is never fully mixed with the oil and stays dry. The פסוק teaches that the מזרק sanctifies even that dry flour. So it does show that a מזרק sanctifies dry items.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It was needed only for the dry part in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing which part of the case the פסוק teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole מנחה is wet, so the פסוק teaches nothing about dry items.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches about the flour in the מנחה that stayed dry.

steps.title: Compared to blood, a מנחה counts as dry
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: next to blood, which is a true liquid, a מנחה counts as dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: A מנחה, compared to blood, is like a dry item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזרק is normally used for blood. Compared with blood, oily flour is still a dry item. So the whole מנחה, not just its unmixed part, shows that a מזרק sanctifies dry items.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say, which brings a second answer
It is like, it counts as

phrases.english: If you want, say:
A meal offering, compared to blood, counts as dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flour mixed with oil counts as a liquid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Compared with blood, a מנחה counts as dry, so the proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: liquid measures do not sanctify dry items, but מזרקות do, because a מנחה, at least compared with blood, counts as dry.

steps.title: שמואל: vessels sanctify only when whole, full, and from inside
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives three conditions for a כלי שרת to sanctify: it must be whole, full, and the item must be inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Service vessels sanctify only when they are whole, only when they are full, and only what is inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new statement with three conditions for when a כלי שרת makes something holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whole means without a hole. Full means it holds the right amount for the offering. From inside means only what is in the vessel becomes holy, not something that just touched its outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Service vessels used in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת – אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא שְׁלֵימִין,
phrases.english: Service vessels sanctify only when whole,
they sanctify only when full,
they sanctify only from inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא שְׁלֵימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement of שמואל, adding conditions for when vessels sanctify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי שרת sanctifies only when it is whole, full, and the item is inside it.

steps.title: Another version of שמואל's statement
steps.stepSummary: Some report שמואל's statement as one combined sentence: vessels sanctify only when whole, full, and from inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: They sanctify only when whole, full, and from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of the same שמואל statement, worded as one combined rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same three conditions appear: whole, full, inside. In the first version each condition was its own clause. Here they are joined into one sentence.

phrases.english: And some say it:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא שְׁלֵימִין וּמְלֵאִים וּמִבִּפְנִים.
phrases.english: They sanctify only when whole, and full, and from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the statement in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels sanctify only when whole, full, and from inside, stated as one combined rule.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, a כלי שרת makes items holy only when it is whole, holds a full measure, and the item is inside it.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two ways of reporting שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two versions of שמואל's rule from steps 13 and 14 lead to any different result. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave three separate conditions, and step 14 gave them as one combined sentence. The גמרא wants to know whether this is only a difference in wording or whether a real case comes out differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two versions of שמואל's statement given just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two versions of שמואל's rule in steps 13 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a real case where the two versions of שמואל's rule give different results?

steps.title: The difference is heaped-up measures
steps.stepSummary: The two versions differ about a heaped-up measure, where the contents rise above the rim of the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is heaped-up measures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions disagree about a vessel filled so high that the contents are heaped up above its rim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'from inside' is its own separate condition, so whatever sticks up above the rim is clearly not made holy. The two ways of saying the rule can treat that heaped-up part differently, so the difference is a real one and not only a matter of wording.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Heaped-up measures, where the contents rise above the vessel's rim

phrases.english: The difference between them is
heaped-up measures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions differ about whether the heaped-up part of a measure above the rim is made holy.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists four conditions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that vessels make an item holy only when it is whole, full, from inside the vessel, and inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: They make items holy only when they are whole, full, from inside them, and inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists all of שמואל's conditions and adds one more: the vessel must be 'inside'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats 'whole', 'full' and 'from inside them', which matches שמואל. It then adds a fourth word, 'inside', which means the vessel makes things holy only inside the עזרה (the Temple courtyard).

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
They make items holy only when whole,
and full, and from inside them, and inside.
phrases.notes: The last word, 'inside', means inside the עזרה. This is a new condition beyond שמואל's three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that matches שמואל's conditions and adds the condition of being inside the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels make items holy only when they are whole, full, from inside the vessel, and inside the עזרה.

steps.title: If he plans to add more, each amount becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the 'full' requirement to a כהן who does not plan to add more; if he does plan to add, each amount becomes holy as soon as it goes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only when he does not plan to add. But if he plans to add, each first amount is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the rule that the vessel must be full. It applies only when the כהן is not planning to put in more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a partly filled vessel does not make its contents holy. But if the כהן intends to keep filling it, the vessel makes each amount holy the moment it goes in, even before the vessel is full. His plan turns the small amount into the start of a full measure.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only when, a phrase that limits a rule
Each amount becomes holy as it goes in

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the כהן's intention can decide when the vessel makes something holy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לְהוֹסִיף,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he does not intend to add,
but if he intends to add,
each first amount is holy.
phrases.notes: Literally 'first, first is holy': every bit becomes holy as soon as it goes in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the 'full' condition from steps 13 and 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'full' requirement applies only when the כהן does not intend to add more. If he intends to add, each amount becomes holy right away.

steps.title: A ברייתא from רבי יוסי supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'full' means a whole amount, and רבי יוסי makes the same limit as רבי יוחנן about a כהן who plans to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: 'Full' means only whole. רבי יוסי said: When is this? When he does not plan to add. But if he plans to add, each first amount is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's limit from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first explains that 'full' simply means a complete measure. Then רבי יוסי, a תנא, says nearly word for word what רבי יוחנן said: the rule applies only when the כהן does not intend to add. So רבי יוחנן's teaching has support from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a ברייתא that supports what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: A vessel needs a full, whole measure to make its contents holy, unless the כהן plans to add more. Then each amount becomes holy as it goes in. This is taught by רבי יוחנן and supported by רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
'Full': 'full' means nothing other than whole.
Rabbi Yosei said: When is this so?
At a time when he does not intend to add;
but if he intends to add,
each first amount is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's limit in step 18 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that if the כהן intends to add, each amount becomes holy right away.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי makes the same distinction.

steps.title: Liquid vessels make dry items holy enough to become פסול
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's rule that a liquid vessel does not make dry items holy, רב (or רב אסי) explains that it does not make them fit for the מזבח, but it does make them able to become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A vessel for liquids does not make holy' and so on. רב said, and some say it was רב אסי: They do not make holy to be offered, but they do make holy to become פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that a vessel for liquids does not make dry items holy, and רב explains exactly what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dry item placed in a liquid vessel cannot be offered on the מזבח because of that vessel. But it is still holy enough that the things which ruin holy items, like being touched by a טבול יום or leaving the עזרה, will make it פסול. So the liquid vessel gives a partial holiness, not none at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as saying the liquid vessel has no effect at all on a dry item. It cannot make the item fit to offer, but it does make it holy enough to become פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two levels of holiness from a vessel: holy enough to be offered, and holy enough only to become פסול.

phrases.english: 'A vessel for liquids does not make holy' and so on.
Rav said, and some say it was Rav Asi:
They do not make holy to be offered,
but they do make holy to become disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new line of the משנה about liquid vessels and dry items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A liquid vessel does not make a dry item fit to be offered, but it does make it holy enough to become פסול.

steps.title: Another version: רב's rule is about offerings brought from a mixture
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב's rule on a different ברייתא. That ברייתא says offerings brought from מדומע, ערלה, or כלאי הכרם do not become holy. רב explains that such an offering is not holy enough to be offered, but it is holy enough to become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רב's statement on this ברייתא: You may not bring מנחות, נסכים, the מנחה that comes with an animal, or ביכורים from a מדומע mixture. You certainly may not bring them from ערלה or כלאי הכרם. If someone did bring them, they are not holy. רב (some say רב אסי) said: they are not holy enough to be offered, but they are holy enough to become פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where רב's rule from the last step belongs. In this version it is attached to a ברייתא about offerings that come from forbidden produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself stays the same: 'not holy to be offered, but holy to become פסול.' Only its setting changes. Here it explains a ברייתא that says 'it is not holy' about an offering made from מדומע, ערלה, or כלאי הכרם. רב reads that as 'not holy enough for the מזבח,' while it still has enough holiness to become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture of regular produce with תְּרוּמָה, which only כהנים may eat
Fruit from a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden to eat
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard
First fruits brought to the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רב's rule here is the same rule as in step 20. The only difference is which ברייתא it is attached to.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב's statement from the step before: not holy to be offered, but holy to become פסול.

phrases.english: One may not bring meal offerings and wine offerings
or the meal offering that comes with an animal, or first fruits
from a mixture containing תרומה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מֵעׇרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם.
phrases.english: and needless to say, not from ערלה or from mixed plantings of a vineyard.
And if he did bring them, they are not holy.
Rav said, and some say it was Rav Asi:
It is not holy enough to be offered,
but it is holy enough to become disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves רב's rule from step 20 onto a different ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering brought from מדומע, ערלה, or כלאי הכרם cannot be offered, but it has enough holiness to become פסול.

steps.title: Damaged holy vessels and knives may not be repaired
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says holy vessels with a hole or a dent may not be fixed. A dented knife may not be sharpened, and a blade that came loose may not be put back. אבא שאול tells of a knife that kept making animals unfit, so the כהנים voted to put it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If holy vessels got a hole, you may not melt them to close it, and you may not melt lead into them. If they got dented, you may not fix them. If a knife got a nick, you may not sharpen away the nick. If the blade came loose, you may not put it back. אבא שאול says: There was a knife in the מקדש that made animals unfit, and the כהנים voted about it and put it away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule about holy vessels with a hole. It quotes a ברייתא about what to do with holy vessels that are damaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of damage gets the same answer: you do not repair it. A hole, a dent, a nicked knife, and a loose blade are all left as they are. אבא שאול adds a real event: a knife that kept making animals unfit was not fixed. The כהנים voted to put it away instead.

keyTerms.meaning: They put it away (took it out of use)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Holy vessels that got a hole –
one may not melt them,
and one may not melt lead into them.
If they got dented, one may not fix them.
A knife that got a nick –
one may not sharpen away its nick.
If it came loose, one may not put it back.
Abba Shaul says:
There was a knife in the מקדש that made animals unfit,
and the כהנים voted about it and put it away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's clause about holy vessels with a hole (step 8) and brings a ברייתא on repairing damaged vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaged holy vessels and knives are not repaired.

steps.title: Priestly clothing must be woven, and dirty clothing is not washed with soap
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says בגדי כהונה must be made by weaving, not by sewing pieces together, based on the פסוק 'מעשה אורג.' If the clothes got dirty, they are not washed with נתר or אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בגדי כהונה are not made by needlework, only by weaving, as it says 'woven work.' If they got dirty, you do not wash them with נתר or with אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time about the כהנים' clothing. It covers how the clothes are made and how dirty clothes are treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two rules. First, the clothes must be woven as whole pieces and not sewn together, because the פסוק says 'מעשה אורג.' Second, clothes that got dirty are not washed with strong cleaners like נתר and אהל. This second rule is what the גמרא questions in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Woven work, made on a loom
A strong cleaning mineral used for washing
A kind of soap made from plants

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Priestly clothing –
one does not make them by needlework,
but only by woven work,
as it says: 'Woven work.'
If they got dirty, one does not wash them
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: not with נתר and not with אהל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ברייתא about Temple items, this time clothing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בגדי כהונה must be woven, and dirty ones are not washed with נתר or אהל.

steps.title: Does this mean dirty clothes may be washed with plain water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the ברייתא's wording. Since it only forbids נתר and אהל, does that mean washing with water is allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean that with water, you may wash them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It points out what the rule seems to imply about washing with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only forbids נתר and אהל for dirty clothes. That suggests plain water would be allowed. The גמרא finds this implication hard to accept, so it questions how the ברייתא should be read.

keyTerms.meaning: But then (introduces a conclusion drawn from the wording)

phrases.english: But then, with water, one may wash them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what the washing rule in step 23 implies
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that dirty בגדי כהונה are not washed with נתר or אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding only נתר and אהל suggests water is allowed for dirty clothes, and the גמרא finds that hard to accept.

steps.title: אביי: lightly dirty clothes may be washed even with soap
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the ברייתא in a new way. Clothes that are only dirty enough to need water are not called 'dirty,' so they may be washed even with נתר and אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the ברייתא means. If the clothes only reached the level of needing water, you may wash them with נתר and אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by explaining how the ברייתא should be read. His explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says the ברייתא is talking about two levels of dirt. If clothes are only lightly dirty, the kind that water alone could clean, they are not treated as 'dirty' at all. Washing them even with נתר and אהל is allowed. So the 'water' the גמרא asked about does not mean water may be used on heavily dirty clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (explaining a source in a new way)

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it means:
If they only reached the level of needing water –
phrases.notes: He means the clothes are so lightly dirty that water alone would clean them.

phrases.english: one may wash them with נתר and אהל;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the ברייתא as talking about different levels of dirt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow washing dirty clothes with water
steps.terutzMaskana: Lightly dirty clothes, the kind water could clean, may be washed even with נתר and אהל.
